items.use_note: Regulatory information, not advice: confirm with a professional.

data.summary: Data collected and processed by external vendors must be protected, not shared without explicit consent or agreement, and made available to the procuring entity on request.
data.regime: Guidelines on Information Security Practices for Government Entities

items.claim: User access deactivation request must be submitted immediately upon termination of employment, non-compliance, suspicious activity, or disciplinary action.
items.use_note: Rule with a value: confirm it before relying on it.

data.statement: User access deactivation request must be submitted immediately upon termination of employment, instances of non-compliance, suspicious activity and in case required as part of disciplinary action.
data.subject: user access
data.value: immediately

items.use_note: Provider option: compare authentication, events, sandbox and limits.

data.need: mobile payment acceptance on a COTS device
data.current_status: current PCI SSC requirements for mobile payment acceptance

items.label: Jugnoo ride payment options
items.claim: Jugnoo riders pay the fare at ride completion in cash, Freecharge, Mobikwik, Paytm or UPI.
items.use_note: Provider option: compare authentication, events, sandbox and limits.

items.label: Requested permissions shown on grant page
items.claim: The permissions an app requests are shown to the merchant on the OAuth grant page, where the merchant can grant or decline them.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Request only the access permissions the app needs, since the merchant sees and can decline them on the OAuth grant page.

items.label: android.permissions only for extra permissions
items.claim: The android.permissions key is only needed for additional permissions that a library does not add by default.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Add a permission with android.permissions only when the library does not already include it by default.

items.label: android permissions set in app config
items.claim: Android permissions are configured with the android.permissions and android.blockedPermissions keys in the app config.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Android permissions must be declared with the android.permissions key in the app config, and unwanted ones blocked with android.blockedPermissions.

items.label: google may reject unjustified dangerous permissions
items.claim: Google may reject apps that use dangerous or signature permissions without valid reasons.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must have valid reasons for any dangerous or signature permission it uses, and should follow Android permission best practices at submission.

items.label: Deprecated APIs block app submission
items.claim: Apps that use APIs which will be deprecated within 90 days cannot be submitted to the Shopify App Store.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Use supported APIs only; apps using APIs that will be deprecated within 90 days cannot be submitted.

items.label: Explain non-obvious features in review notes
items.claim: Include detailed explanations of non-obvious features and in-app purchases in the App Review notes, with supporting documentation where appropriate.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Describe non-obvious features and in-app purchases in App Review notes with supporting documentation.

items.label: No payment requirement for Apple Music access
items.claim: Apps using Apple Music access may not require payment or indirectly monetize access to the Apple Music service, including through in-app purchase.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not require payment or indirectly monetize access to the Apple Music service, such as through in-app purchase or advertising.

items.label: Use Apple Pay branding correctly
items.claim: Apps using Apple Pay must use Apple Pay branding and user interface elements correctly, as described in the Apple Pay Marketing Guidelines and Human Interface Guidelines.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Use Apple Pay branding and user interface elements correctly, as described in the Apple Pay Marketing Guidelines and Human Interface Guidelines.

items.label: Limit sharing of Apple Pay user data
items.claim: Apps using Apple Pay may only share user data acquired via Apple Pay with third parties to facilitate or improve delivery of goods and services.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Share user data acquired via Apple Pay only with third parties to facilitate or improve delivery of goods and services.

items.label: Show purchase information before Apple Pay sale
items.claim: Apps using Apple Pay must provide all material purchase information to the user before any sale of a good or service.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Provide all material purchase information to the user before the sale of any good or service made through Apple Pay.

items.label: Disclose actual charges for recurring payments
items.claim: Apps offering recurring Apple Pay payments must disclose the actual charges that will be billed to the customer.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Disclose the actual charges that will be billed to the customer.

items.label: Disclose renewal term for recurring Apple Pay payments
items.claim: Apps offering recurring Apple Pay payments must disclose the length of the renewal term and that it continues until canceled.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Disclose the length of the renewal term and the fact that it continues until canceled.

items.label: Unsupported authenticator combinations on Android 10 and lower
items.claim: DEVICE_CREDENTIAL alone and BIOMETRIC_STRONG | DEVICE_CREDENTIAL are not supported on Android 10 (API level 29) and lower.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not use DEVICE_CREDENTIAL alone or BIOMETRIC_STRONG | DEVICE_CREDENTIAL as authenticators on Android 10 and lower.

items.label: Add androidx.biometric dependency
items.claim: The app module must add a dependency on the androidx.biometric library in its build.gradle file.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Add a dependency on the androidx.biometric library in the app module build.gradle file.

items.label: Declare DEVICE_CREDENTIAL fallback
items.claim: To allow fallback to device credentials, DEVICE_CREDENTIAL must be included in the values passed to setAllowedAuthenticators().
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Include DEVICE_CREDENTIAL in the set of values passed to setAllowedAuthenticators() to allow device credential fallback.

items.label: Check for PIN or pattern on Android 10
items.claim: On Android 10 and lower, the presence of a PIN, pattern, or password is checked with KeyguardManager.isDeviceSecure().
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Use KeyguardManager.isDeviceSecure() to check for a PIN, pattern, or password on Android 10 and lower.

items.label: Specify key validity time period
items.claim: A secret key allowing biometric or lock screen authentication requires a specified validity time period when configured.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Specify a validity time period when configuring a key that allows biometric or lock screen credential authentication.

items.label: Key requires user authentication for encryption
items.claim: Sensitive information is encrypted only after biometric authentication by generating a key with setUserAuthenticationRequired(true).
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Generate the encryption key with KeyGenParameterSpec and setUserAuthenticationRequired(true).

items.label: Credential Manager for initial sign-in
items.claim: As a general rule, Credential Manager should be used for initial sign-in on a device.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Use Credential Manager for initial sign-in; re-authorizations can use Biometric Prompt or Credential Manager.

items.label: Disable Bluetooth WPAN data synchronization
items.claim: The agency must disable wireless personal area networks that allow a mobile device to connect to a computer via Bluetooth or NFC for data synchronization or storage.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Disable WPAN connections that allow a mobile device to connect to a computer via Bluetooth or NFC for data synchronization or storage.

items.label: Disable Bluetooth when idle
items.claim: Users should disable Bluetooth when it is not actively transmitting information and switch Bluetooth devices to hidden mode.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Disable Bluetooth when not actively transmitting and set Bluetooth devices to hidden mode.

items.label: No FTI transmission via Bluetooth
items.claim: The agency should implement a policy that states FTI must not be transmitted via Bluetooth.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Adopt a policy stating FTI must not be transmitted via Bluetooth.

items.label: Bluetooth enabled and accessory in range
items.claim: Bluetooth must be enabled on the phone, and the accessory must be powered on, within range and compatible with the phone. Initial pairing may still be needed.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The phone's Bluetooth must be enabled and the accessory powered on, within range, compatible and, where requested, confirmed during initial pairing.

items.label: CompanionDeviceService background permissions
items.claim: To start a companion service from the background, an app can use CompanionDeviceService with either REQUEST_COMPANION_RUN_IN_BACKGROUND or REQUEST_COMPANION_START_FOREGROUND_SERVICES_FROM_BACKGROUND permissions.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Declare use of CompanionDeviceService and request either REQUEST_COMPANION_RUN_IN_BACKGROUND or REQUEST_COMPANION_START_FOREGROUND_SERVICES_FROM_BACKGROUND to start the service from the background.

items.label: Keep connection alive with companion presence
items.claim: To keep a connection alive indefinitely, an app can use CompanionDeviceService with REQUEST_COMPANION_RUN_IN_BACKGROUND and CompanionDeviceManager.startObservingDevicePresence().
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Use CompanionDeviceService with REQUEST_COMPANION_RUN_IN_BACKGROUND and call CompanionDeviceManager.startObservingDevicePresence() to keep the connection alive.

items.label: Foreground service started while app visible
items.claim: A connectedDevice foreground service can be started while the app is in the foreground or within one of the exemptions.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Start the connectedDevice foreground service only while the app is in the foreground or within one of the listed exemptions.

rule: Start a foreground service with the connectedDevice foreground service type to keep the peripheral connection alive.

items.label: Bluetooth Connect permission for device management
items.claim: The app lists the Bluetooth Connect permission as required, used to connect and manage Bluetooth devices.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must request the Bluetooth Connect permission to connect and manage Bluetooth devices.

items.label: Bluetooth features vary by Android and hardware
items.claim: The page states that some Bluetooth features may vary depending on Android version, connected device support, and available Bluetooth hardware.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Bluetooth feature availability depends on the Android version, connected device support, and the device's Bluetooth hardware.

items.label: startScan with PendingIntent when process not running
items.claim: When the app process is not running, BluetoothLeScanner can call startScan() with a PendingIntent instead of a ScanCallback to be notified of matching devices.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Use startScan() with a PendingIntent instead of a ScanCallback to be notified of matching devices when the app process is not running.

items.label: BLE scan while app not visible
items.claim: Scanning with BluetoothLeScanner or CompanionDeviceManager has no limitation while the app is not visible, but both need the app process to be alive.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app process must be alive for BLE scanning through BluetoothLeScanner or CompanionDeviceManager; otherwise a workaround is needed.

items.label: Peripheral notifications need connection kept alive
items.claim: Listening to peripheral notifications requires calling setCharacteristicNotification() and keeping the connection alive, and CompanionDeviceService is preferred for long listening periods.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Call setCharacteristicNotification() and keep the connection alive to receive peripheral notifications; CompanionDeviceService is recommended for long listening.

items.label: Bluetooth Scan permission for nearby devices
items.claim: The app lists the Bluetooth Scan permission as required, used to discover nearby Bluetooth devices.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must request the Bluetooth Scan permission to discover nearby Bluetooth devices.

items.label: Location access required for Bluetooth scanning on Android
items.claim: The app states that Location Access is required for Bluetooth scanning on Android.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must request Location Access, which is required for Bluetooth scanning on Android.

items.label: No monetizing built-in device capabilities
items.claim: Apps may not monetize built-in hardware or operating system capabilities such as Push Notifications, the camera, or the gyroscope.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not monetize built-in hardware or operating system capabilities such as Push Notifications, the camera, or the gyroscope.

items.label: Privacy policy must be accessible in app
items.claim: The Privacy Policy must be made easily accessible from within the app itself.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must provide an easily accessible link to its Privacy Policy from within the app.

items.label: Camera permission in manifest
items.claim: Requesting camera permission on Android requires placing a uses-permission element in the app manifest.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must place a uses-permission element for camera in the app manifest.

items.label: Check camera permission status on each access
items.claim: Because consent is only required the first time, the app must check the camera permission status whenever it accesses the camera.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must check the camera permission status each time it accesses the camera.

items.label: Educational UI for camera permission
items.claim: The app must implement an educational UI explaining why it requires camera access.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must implement an educational UI that explains why it requires camera access.

items.label: Camera cannot be monetized as built-in capability
items.claim: Apps may not monetize built-in hardware or operating system capabilities such as the camera.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not monetize the camera or other built-in hardware or operating system capabilities.

items.label: Check camera authorization before capture
items.claim: The app must verify the user's camera authorization status before capturing images, using the AVCaptureDevice authorizationStatus(for:) method.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must check the camera authorization status with AVCaptureDevice authorizationStatus(for:) before capturing images.

items.label: NSCameraUsageDescription key in Info.plist
items.claim: The first step to integrate a consent mechanism into an iOS app is to include the NSCameraUsageDescription key in the Info.plist file.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must include the NSCameraUsageDescription key in its Info.plist file.

items.label: Request camera consent when not determined
items.claim: If camera access has not been authorized, the status is notDetermined and the app should use requestAccess(for:completionHandler:) to request consent again.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: When the camera status is notDetermined, the app must call requestAccess(for:completionHandler:) to request consent.

items.label: Privacy policy required for camera apps
items.claim: Apple has required a Privacy Policy for all apps submitted to its App Store since October 2018.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must have a Privacy Policy to be submitted to the App Store.

items.label: Camera and photo mapping data not for marketing
items.claim: Data gathered from depth or facial mapping tools such as ARKit, Camera APIs, or Photo APIs may not be used for marketing or advertising.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.capability: camera and photo API data use
data.rule: Do not use data gathered from Camera APIs or Photo APIs for marketing, advertising, or use-based data mining.

items.label: localized camera usage description per locale
items.claim: A localized permission message uses the matching usage description key, such as NSCameraUsageDescription, in the ios object of each locale file.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Add the matching usage description key, such as NSCameraUsageDescription, to the ios object of every locale file to show the message in the user's language.

items.label: Kids apps privacy policy and statutes
items.claim: Apps in the Kids Category or collecting personal information from a minor must include a privacy policy and comply with children's privacy statutes.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Include a privacy policy and comply with children's privacy statutes when handling minors' personal data.

items.label: Respect user permission settings for data access
items.claim: Apps must respect the user's permission settings and must not manipulate, trick, or force people to consent to unnecessary data access.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Request only necessary data access and do not manipulate or force users to grant permissions they do not need.

items.label: Developers declare data sharing on listing
items.claim: Developers declare how their app shares data, and the store listing shows this declaration to users.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The developer must declare how the app collects and shares user data, as shown in the store's data safety section.

items.label: Device location is personal and sensitive data
items.claim: Google Play counts device location as personal and sensitive user data, so the User Data policy applies to it.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Treat device location data as personal and sensitive user data subject to the User Data policy and its prominent disclosure and consent requirements.

items.label: Location collection without prominent disclosure is a violation
items.claim: An app that collects device location without a prominent disclosure explaining which feature uses the data is a common policy violation.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Provide a prominent disclosure explaining which feature uses device location data and whether the app uses it in the background.

items.label: Digital goods require Guideline 3.1 payments
items.claim: Software offered under rule 4.7.1 must follow Guideline 3.1 to offer digital goods or services to end users.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Follow Guideline 3.1 to offer digital goods or services to end users.

items.label: Mobile biometric data stored on device
items.claim: Encrypted biometric data for mobile facial verification is stored on the device, while cloud services perform the verification.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Encrypted biometric data must be kept on the device, and verification is performed by cloud services.

items.label: ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION listed as prohibited
items.claim: Google Play lists ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION among the permissions that are prohibited.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not declare or request the ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION permission, since Google Play lists it as prohibited.

items.label: Fingerprint verification requires user consent
items.claim: Fingerprint verification requires a regional fingerprint biometric store, appropriate IAM permissions, user consent, and a compatible fingerprint reader.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must obtain user consent and use a compatible fingerprint reader before fingerprint verification is configured.

items.label: App controls fingerprint prompts
items.claim: The biometric service manages biometric data, while the integrated application controls fingerprint prompts and authorization decisions.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The application must itself control fingerprint prompts and decide whether to allow the operation.

items.label: Foreground Services permission for continuous monitoring
items.claim: The app lists the Foreground Services permission as required for continuous Bluetooth monitoring.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must declare the Foreground Services permission for continuous Bluetooth monitoring.

items.label: User review before new app accesses health data
items.claim: Before a new app can access the user's Health Connect data, the user can review and choose what to share.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: A new app must not get access to the user's health data until the user has reviewed and chosen what to share.

items.label: Declare Health Connect data types for every publishing
items.claim: The Health Connect data type declaration must be completed for all publishing requests, for new apps and for updates that use a different set of data types.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Declare the Health Connect data types the app uses in the Play Console for every new publish and for updates that change the data types used.

items.label: Legacy API Request form users must declare by
items.claim: Developers who used the Google Health Connect API Request form must declare their Health Connect data type uses in the Play Console by January 22, 2025.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Apps previously approved via the Google Health Connect API Request form must declare their data type uses in the Play Console by January 22, 2025.

items.label: Resubmit declaration when data types change
items.claim: If the app gains or drops a Health Connect data type, the Health apps declaration form must be filled out again, including all existing and new features and excluding features no longer needed.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Refill the Health apps declaration form when Health Connect data type requirements change, listing all still-used and new features.

items.label: Do not request unused data types
items.claim: If the app does not require access to specific data types, the developer must not request access to them.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not request Health Connect data types the app does not need.

items.label: Request only necessary Health Connect permissions
items.claim: Apps should only request permissions and access data types that support specific, user-facing health features, and must not request broader access than necessary.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Request only the Health Connect permissions and data types needed for user-facing health features and do not request broader access.

items.label: Justify each Health Connect data type request
items.claim: For each permission requested, the developer must provide a clear and detailed justification explaining how the app uses the data to benefit the user.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Provide a detailed justification in the Health apps form for every Health Connect permission requested.

items.label: Health data not used for targeted ads
items.claim: Ads may not engage in targeted or behavioral advertising based on sensitive user data such as health/medical data from the HealthKit APIs.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Apps must not use HealthKit health or medical data for targeted or behavioral advertising.

items.label: Disclose collected device health data
items.claim: Apps must disclose the specific health data they collect from the device.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Declare the specific health data collected from the device.

items.label: Health data for direct user benefit
items.claim: Apps may use health or fitness data to provide a benefit directly to the user only if submitted by the entity providing the benefit and the data is not shared with a third party.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Use of health data for a user benefit requires submission by the benefit-providing entity and no third-party sharing.

items.label: Health apps declaration form required for publishing
items.claim: To publish a health app on Google Play, the developer must fill out the Health Apps declaration form in the Play Console.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must complete the Health Apps declaration form in the Play Console before publishing.

items.label: Health research needs ethics board approval
items.claim: Apps conducting health-related human subject research must secure approval from an independent ethics review board and provide proof upon request.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Obtain approval from an independent ethics review board and provide proof upon request for health-related human subject research.

items.label: No false data written to HealthKit
items.claim: Apps must not write false or inaccurate data into HealthKit or other medical research or health management apps.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not write false or inaccurate data into HealthKit.

items.label: No personal health information in iCloud
items.claim: Apps may not store personal health information in iCloud.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not store personal health information in iCloud.

items.label: Commission invoice payment within 30 days
items.claim: Apple calculates commissions by the 15th of the following month and developers must pay within 30 days of receiving the invoice.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Pay the monthly commission invoice within 30 days of receiving it.

items.label: Developer handles support for alternative payments
items.claim: Apple cannot assist customers with refunds, purchase history or subscription management for alternative payment purchases, so the developer must provide timely support.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Provide timely customer support for refunds, purchase history, subscription management and other issues on alternative payments.

items.label: StoreKit external purchases entitlement required
items.claim: Apps offering alternative payment options in Japan must include the StoreKit External Purchases or Offers Entitlement.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must include the StoreKit External Purchases or Offers Entitlement when using alternative payment options.

items.label: Track and report alternative payment transactions
items.claim: Developers using alternative payments must track and send Apple a report of all alternative payment transactions for commission calculation.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Track and report all alternative payment transactions to Apple for commission calculation and collection.

items.label: Developer responsible for taxes on alternative payments
items.claim: For purchases that do not use Apple In-App Purchase, the developer is responsible for collecting and remitting applicable taxes for sales processed by an alternative payment provider.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Collect and remit applicable taxes for alternative payment sales processed by an alternative payment provider.

items.label: Apple IAP on every merchandising screen
items.claim: Apple In-App Purchase must be provided on every screen where the app merchandises a digital good and offers a payment option.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Provide Apple In-App Purchase as an option on every screen that merchandises a digital good or service and offers a payment option.

items.label: Apple In-App Purchase must be offered alongside alternatives
items.claim: If an app offers an alternative payment option, Apple In-App Purchase must also be presented as an option.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Present Apple In-App Purchase as an option whenever an alternative payment option is offered for digital goods and services.

items.label: Apple In-App Purchase displayed at least as prominently
items.claim: Apple In-App Purchase must be displayed at least as prominently as any other payment option shown.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Display Apple In-App Purchase at least as prominently as any other payment option shown.

items.label: 21% commission on alternative payment sales
items.claim: Apple charges a 21% commission on sales of digital goods or services, including those using alternative payments within apps, excluding certain program participants and renewals.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Pay Apple a 21% commission on sales of digital goods or services made with alternative payments within the app.

items.label: Custom purchase link entitlement key for Japan
items.claim: The entitlement key com.apple.developer.storekit.custom-purchase-link.allowed-regions must be set as an array of strings with the value jp.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Add the entitlement key com.apple.developer.storekit.custom-purchase-link.allowed-regions as an array of strings with value jp in the entitlements property list.

items.label: Entitlement usable on iOS 26.2 Japan storefront
items.claim: The entitlement profile may only be used in apps on the Japan storefront on iPhone running iOS 26.2 or later.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Use the entitlement profile only in apps on the Japan storefront on iPhone running iOS 26.2 or later.

items.label: External links allowed for non-digital goods
items.claim: For non-digital goods or services such as physical products, memberships, or event tickets, external payment links are allowed according to the article.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: External payment links may be used for non-digital goods or services such as physical products, memberships, or event tickets.

items.label: Apple bans external purchase links for digital goods
items.claim: Apple's guidelines state apps may not include buttons, links, or calls-to-action that direct customers to purchasing mechanisms other than In-App Purchase.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must not include buttons, links or calls-to-action that send customers to purchasing mechanisms other than In-App Purchase.

items.label: Alternative PSP must meet PCI Level 1
items.claim: An alternative payment service provider must meet Level 1 PCI compliance for handling credit and debit card data.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The alternative payment service provider must meet Level 1 PCI compliance for handling credit and debit card data.

items.label: PSP name in review notes
items.claim: If an alternative payment service provider is used, its name should be included in the App Review notes.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Include the name of the alternative payment service provider in the review notes at submission.

items.label: Webviews and redirects to checkout risk rejection
items.claim: Attempts to work around restrictions with webviews, deep links, or browser redirects could result in rejection.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must avoid using webviews, deep links or browser redirects to get around the in-app payment restrictions.

items.label: Charge app costs through Shopify billing
items.claim: Shopify apps should charge other app costs through Shopify's app billing system, while a PCI-compliant gateway is used for goods sold to merchants.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Charge other app costs through Shopify's app billing system and use a PCI-compliant gateway only for goods sold to merchants.

items.label: Unclear in-app purchases can reject review
items.claim: If in-app purchases are not immediately obvious to the reviewer, the review is delayed and may trigger a rejection.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Make the business model and in-app purchases obvious and explain them in metadata and App Review notes to avoid review delay or rejection.

items.label: Indicate additional purchases in app metadata
items.claim: Apps with in-app purchases must clearly indicate in the description, screenshots, and previews whether featured items, levels, or subscriptions require additional purchases.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app description, screenshots, and previews must clearly indicate whether featured items, levels, or subscriptions require additional purchases.

items.label: Explain unreviewable in-app purchase items
items.claim: If any configured in-app purchase items cannot be found or reviewed in the app, the reason must be explained in the review notes.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Explain in the review notes why any configured in-app purchase item cannot be found or reviewed in the app.

items.label: Explain non-obvious in-app purchases in review notes
items.claim: Non-obvious features and in-app purchases must be explained in the App Review notes, with supporting documentation where appropriate.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Explain non-obvious features and in-app purchases in the App Review notes, adding supporting documentation where appropriate.

items.label: Communicate which content needs purchases
items.claim: Apps offering creator content must communicate to users which content requires additional purchases.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Communicate to users which creator content requires additional purchases.

items.label: infoPlist changes need a new native binary
items.claim: Changes to the Info.plist cannot be updated over-the-air and are only deployed when a new native binary is submitted.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Any change to Info.plist permission messages requires a new native binary build and submission rather than an over-the-air update.

items.label: default permission messages may fail app store review
items.claim: Default permission messages will most likely need tailoring to the app's use case to be accepted by the App Store.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Replace the default permission messages with text tailored to the app's specific use case before App Store submission.

items.label: Android permissions set in app config
items.claim: On Android, permissions are configured with the android.permissions and android.blockedPermissions keys in the app config.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Declare Android permissions under android.permissions and remove unwanted ones with android.blockedPermissions in the app config.

items.label: Native config needed for standalone builds
items.claim: Permissions in standalone and development builds require native build-time configuration before they can be requested using runtime JavaScript code.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must configure permissions natively at build time before requesting them in JavaScript.

items.label: OS blocks repeat permission prompts
items.claim: Android and iOS prohibit an app from asking for the same permission more than once, so testing rejection flows may require reinstalling the native app.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app cannot re-request a permission already answered; reinstall the native app to retest permission flows.

items.label: Ask user permission before sensitive access
items.claim: The app must request the user's permission first before accessing potentially sensitive information such as location or contacts.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must request the user's permission at runtime before accessing sensitive data such as location.

items.label: Improper permission setup risks rejection
items.claim: If native permissions are not configured or explained properly, the app may be rejected or pulled from the stores.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must configure and explain native permissions properly to avoid store rejection or removal.

items.label: Native config not needed in Expo Go
items.claim: Native build-time permission configuration is not required when testing projects in the Expo Go app.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Native build-time permission configuration is not needed when testing in Expo Go.

items.label: Info.plist changes need new native binary
items.claim: Changes to the Info.plist cannot be updated over-the-air and are deployed only when a new native binary is submitted.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Changes to Info.plist permission messages require submitting a new native binary rather than an over-the-air update.

items.label: iOS permission messages in infoPlist
items.claim: On iOS, permission messages are set with the ios.infoPlist key in the app config, and default messages will most likely need to be tailored for App Store acceptance.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must declare iOS permission usage messages via ios.infoPlist and tailor default messages to its use case.

items.label: No location APIs for emergency or vehicle control
items.claim: Location-based APIs must not be used to provide emergency services or autonomous control over vehicles, aircraft, and other devices, except small devices such as lightweight drones and toys.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not use location-based APIs to provide emergency services or autonomous control over vehicles, aircraft, and other devices, except small devices such as lightweight drones and toys.

items.label: Notify and obtain consent before location use
items.claim: The app must notify the user and obtain consent before collecting, transmitting, or using location data.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Notify the user and obtain consent before collecting, transmitting, or using location data.

items.label: Explain location purpose in the app
items.claim: If the app uses Location Services, it must explain the purpose of that use within the app.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Explain the purpose of Location Services use inside the app.

items.label: Location Services only when relevant
items.claim: Apps must use Location Services only when it is directly relevant to the features and services the app provides.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Request and use Location Services only when directly relevant to the app's features and services.

items.label: No forced enabling of location or tracking
items.claim: Apps may not require users to enable system functionalities such as location services or tracking in order to access app functionality.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not require users to enable location services or tracking to access functionality, content, or use of the app.

items.label: MDM app analytics restriction
items.claim: Third-party analytics in MDM apps may only collect data about the performance of the developer's MDM app, not user or device data.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Limit third-party analytics in MDM apps to performance data of the app itself.

items.label: No background listening or always-on microphone
items.claim: Privacy safeguards prohibit background listening and always-on microphone access for voice biometrics.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must avoid background listening and always-on microphone access when using voice biometrics.

items.label: Disable NFC when idle
items.claim: NFC pairing should be disabled when it is not actively transmitting information, and FTI must not be transmitted via NFC.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Disable NFC pairing when not actively transmitting and adopt a policy that FTI must not be transmitted via NFC.

items.label: Notifications permission for Bluetooth alerts
items.claim: The app lists the Notifications permission as required for Bluetooth alerts and status updates.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must request the Notifications permission to show Bluetooth alerts and status updates.

items.label: No auto-fulfil of pending payment orders
items.claim: Shopify apps should not automatically fulfill orders that are in pending payment state, to protect against fraud risk.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not automatically fulfill orders in pending payment state.

items.label: os blocks repeated permission prompts
items.claim: Android and iOS prohibit an app from asking for the same permission more than once at the operating-system level.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app cannot re-prompt for a permission after the user rejects it, so testing rejected flows may need the native app reinstalled.

items.label: Clear purpose strings for data use
items.claim: Purpose strings must clearly and completely describe the app's use of the data.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Write purpose strings that clearly and completely describe the use of the requested data.

items.label: Expo Go skips native permission config
items.claim: Native build-time permission configuration is not required when testing projects in the Expo Go app.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Native build-time permission configuration is not needed while testing a project in the Expo Go app.

items.label: standalone and dev builds need native config
items.claim: Permissions in standalone and development builds require native build-time configuration before they can be requested at runtime.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Standalone and development builds must include native build-time permission configuration before the app requests the permission in JavaScript.

items.label: Request only data needed for core function
items.claim: Apps should only request access to data relevant to the core functionality and collect only data required for the task.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Request only the data relevant to core functionality.

items.label: No contact database from Photos data
items.claim: Apps must not use information from Contacts, Photos, or other user-data APIs to build a contact database for their own use or for sale or distribution.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not use Photos or Contacts data to build a contact database for your own use or for sale or distribution to third parties.

items.label: Use out-of-process picker or share sheet for Photos
items.claim: Where possible, apps should use the out-of-process picker or a share sheet instead of requesting full access to protected resources such as Photos.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Prefer the out-of-process picker or a share sheet over requesting full access to Photos where possible.

items.label: Saving media needs separate permission
items.claim: Saving media to the device requires a separate permission from camera access.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must request a separate permission to save media to the device.

items.label: No microphone access required to upload photos
items.claim: An app that lets users post photos to a social network must not also require microphone access before allowing photo uploads.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not require microphone access as a condition for uploading photos; provide alternatives for users who do not grant consent where possible.

items.label: Privacy policy must match Health Connect link
items.claim: The app's privacy policy must be posted on its Play store page and must be the same policy shown to users when they click the privacy policy link in Health Connect.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Post the app privacy policy on the Play store page and use the identical policy linked from Health Connect.

items.label: Privacy policy link in metadata and app
items.claim: All apps must include a link to their privacy policy in App Store Connect metadata and within the app.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Include a privacy policy link in App Store Connect metadata and inside the app.

items.label: Cannot require push enablement for access
items.claim: The app may not require users to enable system functionalities such as push notifications in order to access functionality or content.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not require users to enable push notifications to access functionality, content, use of the app, or compensation.

items.label: Provide in-app push opt-out method
items.claim: The app must provide a method for users to opt out of promotional push messages.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Provide an in-app method for users to opt out of receiving promotional push notifications.

items.label: Promotional push requires explicit opt-in
items.claim: Push notifications for promotions or direct marketing require that customers have explicitly opted in.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Use push notifications for promotions or direct marketing only after customers explicitly opt in via consent language displayed in the app UI.

items.label: Push notifications cannot be monetized
items.claim: Built-in capabilities such as Push Notifications may not be monetized by the app.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not monetize push notifications or other built-in hardware or OS capabilities.

items.label: Push notifications misuse leads to rejection
items.claim: Apps that disrupt the operating system or hardware features, including through Push Notifications, will be rejected by App Review.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must not transmit viruses, files, code or programs that harm or disrupt normal operation of the OS or hardware features, including push notifications.

items.label: Background restricted permission use needs full disclosure
items.claim: Using restricted permissions in the background for tracking, research, or marketing without comprehensive disclosure and consent is a common violation.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Do not use restricted permissions in the background for tracking, research, or marketing without comprehensively disclosing the use and obtaining consent.

items.label: Disclosure must precede runtime permission request
items.claim: An in-app prominent disclosure must immediately precede any in-app consent request or runtime permission request.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Show an in-app prominent disclosure immediately before every runtime permission request or in-app consent request.

items.label: Developer responsible for third-party SDK compliance
items.claim: The developer is responsible for ensuring everything in the app complies with the guidelines, including third-party SDKs, so they must be reviewed and chosen carefully.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Review and choose third-party SDKs carefully, since the developer is responsible for their compliance with the guidelines.

items.label: Explicit permission via ATT before tracking
items.claim: Apps must receive explicit user permission through the App Tracking Transparency APIs before tracking user activity.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Request explicit user permission through the App Tracking Transparency APIs before tracking the user's activity.

items.label: Consent before collecting user data
items.claim: Apps that collect user or usage data must secure user consent for the collection, even if the data is anonymous.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Secure user consent before collecting user or usage data, and provide an easy way to withdraw consent.

items.label: Data safety section must be completed
items.claim: Developers must provide information for Google Play's Data safety section as part of the app publishing process.
items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must provide Data safety section information covering data collection, sharing and security practices.

platform_constraints.rule: Provide timely customer support for refunds, purchase history, subscription management and other issues on alternative payments.
The app must include the StoreKit External Purchases or Offers Entitlement when using alternative payment options.
Track and report all alternative payment transactions to Apple for commission calculation and collection.
Collect and remit applicable taxes for alternative payment sales processed by an alternative payment provider.
Provide Apple In-App Purchase as an option on every screen that merchandises a digital good or service and offers a payment option.
Present Apple In-App Purchase as an option whenever an alternative payment option is offered for digital goods and services.
Display Apple In-App Purchase at least as prominently as any other payment option shown.
Pay Apple a 21% commission on sales of digital goods or services made with alternative payments within the app.
Add the entitlement key com.apple.developer.storekit.custom-purchase-link.allowed-regions as an array of strings with value jp in the entitlements property list.
Use the entitlement profile only in apps on the Japan storefront on iPhone running iOS 26.2 or later.
The alternative payment service provider must meet Level 1 PCI compliance for handling credit and debit card data.
Include the name of the alternative payment service provider in the review notes at submission.
Make the business model and in-app purchases obvious and explain them in metadata and App Review notes to avoid review delay or rejection.
The app description, screenshots, and previews must clearly indicate whether featured items, levels, or subscriptions require additional purchases.
Explain in the review notes why any configured in-app purchase item cannot be found or reviewed in the app.
Explain non-obvious features and in-app purchases in the App Review notes, adding supporting documentation where appropriate.
External payment links may be used for non-digital goods or services such as physical products, memberships, or event tickets.
The app must not include buttons, links or calls-to-action that send customers to purchasing mechanisms other than In-App Purchase.
The app must avoid using webviews, deep links or browser redirects to get around the in-app payment restrictions.
Communicate to users which creator content requires additional purchases.
Charge other app costs through Shopify's app billing system and use a PCI-compliant gateway only for goods sold to merchants.
Pay the monthly commission invoice within 30 days of receiving it.
Do not require users to enable push notifications to access functionality, content, use of the app, or compensation.
Provide an in-app method for users to opt out of receiving promotional push notifications.
Use push notifications for promotions or direct marketing only after customers explicitly opt in via consent language displayed in the app UI.
Do not monetize push notifications or other built-in hardware or OS capabilities.
The app must not transmit viruses, files, code or programs that harm or disrupt normal operation of the OS or hardware features, including push notifications.
The app must request the Notifications permission to show Bluetooth alerts and status updates.
Do not require users to enable location services or tracking to access functionality, content, or use of the app.
Request explicit user permission through the App Tracking Transparency APIs before tracking the user's activity.
Do not monetize the camera or other built-in hardware or operating system capabilities.
Do not use data gathered from Camera APIs or Photo APIs for marketing, advertising, or use-based data mining.
Do not require microphone access as a condition for uploading photos; provide alternatives for users who do not grant consent where possible.
The app must check the camera authorization status with AVCaptureDevice authorizationStatus(for:) before capturing images.
The app must include the NSCameraUsageDescription key in its Info.plist file.
When the camera status is notDetermined, the app must call requestAccess(for:completionHandler:) to request consent.
The app must have a Privacy Policy to be submitted to the App Store.
The app must place a uses-permission element for camera in the app manifest.
The app must check the camera permission status each time it accesses the camera.
The app must implement an educational UI that explains why it requires camera access.
The app must provide an easily accessible link to its Privacy Policy from within the app.
Do not use Photos or Contacts data to build a contact database for your own use or for sale or distribution to third parties.
Do not use DEVICE_CREDENTIAL alone or BIOMETRIC_STRONG | DEVICE_CREDENTIAL as authenticators on Android 10 and lower.
Add a dependency on the androidx.biometric library in the app module build.gradle file.
Include DEVICE_CREDENTIAL in the set of values passed to setAllowedAuthenticators() to allow device credential fallback.
Use KeyguardManager.isDeviceSecure() to check for a PIN, pattern, or password on Android 10 and lower.
Use Credential Manager for initial sign-in; re-authorizations can use Biometric Prompt or Credential Manager.
The phone's Bluetooth must be enabled and the accessory powered on, within range, compatible and, where requested, confirmed during initial pairing.
Declare use of CompanionDeviceService and request either REQUEST_COMPANION_RUN_IN_BACKGROUND or REQUEST_COMPANION_START_FOREGROUND_SERVICES_FROM_BACKGROUND to start the service from the background.
Use CompanionDeviceService with REQUEST_COMPANION_RUN_IN_BACKGROUND and call CompanionDeviceManager.startObservingDevicePresence() to keep the connection alive.
Start the connectedDevice foreground service only while the app is in the foreground or within one of the listed exemptions.
Disable WPAN connections that allow a mobile device to connect to a computer via Bluetooth or NFC for data synchronization or storage.
Disable Bluetooth when not actively transmitting and set Bluetooth devices to hidden mode.
Adopt a policy stating FTI must not be transmitted via Bluetooth.
The app must request the Bluetooth Connect permission to connect and manage Bluetooth devices.
Apps must not use HealthKit health or medical data for targeted or behavioral advertising.
Declare the specific health data collected from the device.
Use of health data for a user benefit requires submission by the benefit-providing entity and no third-party sharing.
Include a privacy policy link in App Store Connect metadata and inside the app.
A new app must not get access to the user's health data until the user has reviewed and chosen what to share.
Declare the Health Connect data types the app uses in the Play Console for every new publish and for updates that change the data types used.
Apps previously approved via the Google Health Connect API Request form must declare their data type uses in the Play Console by January 22, 2025.
Refill the Health apps declaration form when Health Connect data type requirements change, listing all still-used and new features.
The app must complete the Health Apps declaration form in the Play Console before publishing.
Post the app privacy policy on the Play store page and use the identical policy linked from Health Connect.
Include a privacy policy and comply with children's privacy statutes when handling minors' personal data.
Request only the data relevant to core functionality.
Do not declare or request the ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION permission, since Google Play lists it as prohibited.
Native build-time permission configuration is not needed while testing a project in the Expo Go app.
Standalone and development builds must include native build-time permission configuration before the app requests the permission in JavaScript.
Request only the access permissions the app needs, since the merchant sees and can decline them on the OAuth grant page.
Add a permission with android.permissions only when the library does not already include it by default.
The app must have valid reasons for any dangerous or signature permission it uses, and should follow Android permission best practices at submission.
Android permissions must be declared with the android.permissions key in the app config, and unwanted ones blocked with android.blockedPermissions.
Use supported APIs only; apps using APIs that will be deprecated within 90 days cannot be submitted.
Describe non-obvious features and in-app purchases in App Review notes with supporting documentation.
Do not require payment or indirectly monetize access to the Apple Music service, such as through in-app purchase or advertising.
Use Apple Pay branding and user interface elements correctly, as described in the Apple Pay Marketing Guidelines and Human Interface Guidelines.
Share user data acquired via Apple Pay only with third parties to facilitate or improve delivery of goods and services.
Provide all material purchase information to the user before the sale of any good or service made through Apple Pay.
Disclose the actual charges that will be billed to the customer.
Disclose the length of the renewal term and the fact that it continues until canceled.
Specify a validity time period when configuring a key that allows biometric or lock screen credential authentication.
Generate the encryption key with KeyGenParameterSpec and setUserAuthenticationRequired(true).
Bluetooth feature availability depends on the Android version, connected device support, and the device's Bluetooth hardware.
Use startScan() with a PendingIntent instead of a ScanCallback to be notified of matching devices when the app process is not running.
The app process must be alive for BLE scanning through BluetoothLeScanner or CompanionDeviceManager; otherwise a workaround is needed.
Call setCharacteristicNotification() and keep the connection alive to receive peripheral notifications; CompanionDeviceService is recommended for long listening.
The app must request the Bluetooth Scan permission to discover nearby Bluetooth devices.
The app must request Location Access, which is required for Bluetooth scanning on Android.
Do not monetize built-in hardware or operating system capabilities such as Push Notifications, the camera, or the gyroscope.
Add the matching usage description key, such as NSCameraUsageDescription, to the ios object of every locale file to show the message in the user's language.
Request only necessary data access and do not manipulate or force users to grant permissions they do not need.
The developer must declare how the app collects and shares user data, as shown in the store's data safety section.
Provide a prominent disclosure explaining which feature uses device location data and whether the app uses it in the background.
Treat device location data as personal and sensitive user data subject to the User Data policy and its prominent disclosure and consent requirements.
Follow Guideline 3.1 to offer digital goods or services to end users.
Encrypted biometric data must be kept on the device, and verification is performed by cloud services.
The app must obtain user consent and use a compatible fingerprint reader before fingerprint verification is configured.
The application must itself control fingerprint prompts and decide whether to allow the operation.
The app must declare the Foreground Services permission for continuous Bluetooth monitoring.
Do not request Health Connect data types the app does not need.
Request only the Health Connect permissions and data types needed for user-facing health features and do not request broader access.
Provide a detailed justification in the Health apps form for every Health Connect permission requested.
Obtain approval from an independent ethics review board and provide proof upon request for health-related human subject research.
Do not write false or inaccurate data into HealthKit.
Do not store personal health information in iCloud.
Any change to Info.plist permission messages requires a new native binary build and submission rather than an over-the-air update.
Replace the default permission messages with text tailored to the app's specific use case before App Store submission.
The app cannot re-request a permission already answered; reinstall the native app to retest permission flows.
The app must request the user's permission at runtime before accessing sensitive data such as location.
The app must configure and explain native permissions properly to avoid store rejection or removal.
The app must configure permissions natively at build time before requesting them in JavaScript.
Changes to Info.plist permission messages require submitting a new native binary rather than an over-the-air update.
The app must declare iOS permission usage messages via ios.infoPlist and tailor default messages to its use case.
Declare Android permissions under android.permissions and remove unwanted ones with android.blockedPermissions in the app config.
Native build-time permission configuration is not needed when testing in Expo Go.
Do not use location-based APIs to provide emergency services or autonomous control over vehicles, aircraft, and other devices, except small devices such as lightweight drones and toys.
Notify the user and obtain consent before collecting, transmitting, or using location data.
Explain the purpose of Location Services use inside the app.
Request and use Location Services only when directly relevant to the app's features and services.
Limit third-party analytics in MDM apps to performance data of the app itself.
The app must avoid background listening and always-on microphone access when using voice biometrics.
Disable NFC pairing when not actively transmitting and adopt a policy that FTI must not be transmitted via NFC.
Do not automatically fulfill orders in pending payment state.
The app cannot re-prompt for a permission after the user rejects it, so testing rejected flows may need the native app reinstalled.
Write purpose strings that clearly and completely describe the use of the requested data.
Prefer the out-of-process picker or a share sheet over requesting full access to Photos where possible.
The app must request a separate permission to save media to the device.
Do not use restricted permissions in the background for tracking, research, or marketing without comprehensively disclosing the use and obtaining consent.
Show an in-app prominent disclosure immediately before every runtime permission request or in-app consent request.
Review and choose third-party SDKs carefully, since the developer is responsible for their compliance with the guidelines.
Secure user consent before collecting user or usage data, and provide an easy way to withdraw consent.
The app must provide Data safety section information covering data collection, sharing and security practices.

## COMPLIANCE NOTES (information, not advice)
consent for vehicle and driver tracking: Customers are responsible for getting any legally required consent before tracking a vehicle or a driver's phone.
e-invoice QR code signing by IRPs: Only e-invoices with QR codes signed by IRPs conforming to the e-invoicing standards under the GST Act and rules can be verified by the app.
e-invoicing: E-Invoices for B2B transactions are mandatory for businesses with turnover above ₹5 Crores.
e-way bill: E-Way Bills must be created for goods movement exceeding ₹50,000.
personal data processing roles: The customer is the Data Fiduciary and FleetVeda is Data Processor for personal data in customer data; the customer must have a lawful basis and tell drivers, staff and customers how data is used.
reconciliation: A reconciliation framework covering payment system operators, card networks, aggregators, gateways and other participants must operate in real time or within 24 hours of receiving settlement files.
restricted business categories for WhatsApp Business API: Companies that deal in illegal products and services, unsafe indigestible supplements, alcohol etc. are restricted from procuring the WhatsApp Business API, per the WhatsApp Legal Commerce Policy.
